summary: Before the International Space Station, the Soviet Union and the United States built and tested earlier space stations, including Salyut, Skylab, and Mir, learning hard lessons along the way.
introduce: Write the key term “module” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to guess what it means. Share a few guesses, then tell students to find the word in “Space Stations Before the ISS” and check whether they were right.

keyTerms.def: a separate section that can be joined to other sections to make a larger structure
a special job or task that a person or team is sent to do
the best or most of something ever achieved

challengeTerms.def: the length of time that something lasts
a sudden and forceful crash between two moving objects
to change something from one form or use into another

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that building the very first space station was harder than building the ISS? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Choose one lesson that engineers learned from an early space station.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review module, mission, and record, and let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses duration, collision, and convert to teach the class one of the terms with their own example.
